title: Issue #230: Native implementation backlog from competitive monitoring — Aurora, ShivaCore, Wallet and Factories
content:
State: open

## Objective

Convert the accepted competitive-monitoring findings into native A-TownChain/ShivaCore capabilities. Adopt concepts and requirements, not proprietary source code or mandatory third-party runtime services.

**Architecture rule:** Standalone First · Native Implementation · Ecosystem Second.

## Implementation order

### P0 — authority, enforcement, wallet and evidence
- [ ] Review the normative catalog and bind every item to its existing component SSOT before coding.
- [ ] Aurora Authority Plane: agent identity, capability grants, delegation, approval, policy versioning and revocation.
- [ ] Aurora Runtime + ShivaCore: per-agent isolation, tool/action allowlists, resource/network/filesystem/IPC boundaries, fail-closed enforcement and revocation tests.
- [ ] Wallet SSOT: transaction simulation, limits, destination/contract allowlists, risk-based approvals and signing authorization that agents cannot bypass.
- [ ] atc-engineering / a-townchain-ecosystem: exact-head evidence, run/job/step provenance, artifact SHA-256 and BLOCKED handling for missing or mismatched evidence.

### P1 — durable agents and native factories
- [ ] Aurora task lifecycle: durable state, checkpoint/resume, cancellation, bounded retries, idempotency, versioned skills and memory provenance.
- [ ] Identify the authoritative SSOT repositories for AI Franchise Factory, Research Factory and Business Factory before implementation.
- [ ] Native process/context graph: versioned process, role, rule, control and evidence relationships with source provenance and freshness.
- [ ] Native factory lifecycle: idea → research → validation → production → release → monitoring, with approval gates and artifact lineage.
- [ ] Local-first inference/model routing in Aurora AI; optional remote inference must be explicitly scoped and never required for core operation.

### P2 — evaluation and GlobusOS integration
- [ ] Identify the SSOT for agent evaluation before adding a new test harness.
- [ ] Measure task success, policy violations, revocation latency, sandbox escape resistance, resource exhaustion, audit completeness and recovery.
- [ ] GlobusOS desktop controls for approval, agent status, capability visibility, audit and kill/revoke; UI is not the enforcement boundary.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every item has NATIVE_BUILD_CANDIDATE, TARGET_SSOT, ARCHITECTURE_GAP, IMPLEMENTATION_PRIORITY, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA, EXTERNAL_RUNTIME_DEPENDENCY=false and EVIDENCE_STATUS.
- No duplicated core implementation in a-townchain-ecosystem.
- Negative security tests and component-specific tests pass.
- Evidence is tied to exact commit SHA and relevant paths/symbols/blob SHAs; Actions run → job → step evidence and artifact hashes are recorded.
- Unknown SSOT, missing evidence, or failing tests is BLOCKED; green CI alone is not VERIFIED.
- No merge or VERIFIED claim until the applicable governance/security gates and exact-head evidence pass.

## Evidence inputs
- ServiceNow Arc / NVIDIA: long-running task ownership, action-level authorization, runtime containment and revocation are design patterns only; AI Passport hardware/runtime enforcement remains future availability per the official announcement.
- Oracle Fusion Claw: deterministic execution, human approvals and auditable outcome receipts.
- ARIS Process Context: versioned process context and provenance; verify live availability before relying on it.
- Ethereum Glamsterdam/Hoodi postponement: revocable activation schedules and stale-target withdrawal.
- Windows/Linux release-health findings: external regression-test inspiration, not evidence of existing GlobusOS defects.

## Governance
Catalog First, Implementation Second. This issue is a planning/control record, not implementation evidence. Keep the monitoring PR Draft until its own acceptance checks are independently verified.
